column4: why this decision is worth a row

column1: # `tests` is space-separated and names the test that ASSERTS the decision — not
# every test that happens to break under the mutation.

column4: a shallow checkout read as full makes every ancestry answer a maybe, and the walk grades itself on a truncated history instead of saying so
the walk must ACT on shallowness, not merely observe it: a shallow checkout read as full grades the release on a truncated history and hands down the verdict green instead of failing loud

exec.CommandContext KILLS git on cancel and a killed child is an ordinary ExitError, so reading the exit status first swallows a Ctrl-C into "this commit never landed" — a wrong answer about which commits a release counts, returned with a nil error

cat-file --batch-check answers "<sha> missing" for an object the repository does not hold, so trusting the line without checking it says `commit` claims a sha that is not there and the footprint places a commit that never landed

git keeps a unit separator inside an author name, so git log fields framed by one let a contributor choose where the next field starts: `dependabot[bot]<US>x` read as dependabot[bot], its email as the parents and its parents as the message (t-esm5)

the gate half: a commit whose author only reads as the bot once the fields shift was excluded from lint at exit 0 — measured with an ordinary, an empty and a 40-hex email, the last two passing a check of the parents field alone

a record is believed only when the two fields git alone writes — the SHA and the parents — are object names; without the check a record whose fields did not land where the format put them reaches every gate as a commit by the wrong author instead of failing the read at 4

a SHA-256 repository names its objects with 64 hex digits and glyph read one before the record check existed (lint 3 on a violation, bump v0.0.1, measured), so a check wired to SHA-1's 40 refuses every commit there at exit 4

under log.showSignature git prints each signature's verdict on stdout ahead of the commit's record, --format or not, and the record check refuses any byte outside a record, so without --no-show-signature every history read of a developer who signs fails at 4 (measured on git 2.54)

the gates half: lint --range, bump, notes and the pre-push hook answered 4 instead of judging a signing developer's commits, and the installed pre-push hook lets 4 through — a violation pushed to the default branch went out unjudged (measured)

i18n.logOutputEncoding re-encodes what git log prints: without --encoding=UTF-8 an author and a message arrive as Latin-1 bytes under ISO-8859-1, and under UTF-16 the whole record does, which the record check refuses — every history read fails at 4 (measured on git 2.54)

the gates half: under UTF-16 lint --range, bump, notes and the pre-push hook answered 4 instead of judging, and the installed pre-push hook lets 4 through; under ISO-8859-1 notes wrote the subject's Latin-1 bytes into the release body (measured)

diff-tree's %P header is pretty-printed, so i18n.logOutputEncoding re-encodes it too: under UTF-16 the header is cut at its own first NUL and the parent's hex digits come back as the commit's file list (measured on git 2.54)
column.ui=always (or column.tag) columns git tag --list even into a pipe: without --no-column every tag on a row is read as one name that parses as no version (measured on git 2.54)

the verdict half: with the tag list read as one name the step base falls to v0.0.0 — bump --range printed v0.0.1 at exit 0 with nothing said where the answer is v0.1.1, and a bare --since-tag warned that HEAD's history holds no version tag and walked the whole of it (measured)

git records a cleaned message with a closing newline the hook's text never has, and Go's `$` matches only at the end of the text, so a pattern ending in `$` passes a one-line subject at the commit-msg hook and refuses the same commit at lint --range and bump --range (t-3p3k, measured)
Message is git's message minus the one newline git records it with — the shape cleanup.Apply hands the hook — or every history reader judges a different text than the authoring path did

only git's closing newline is the record's: a verbatim message keeps the trailing blank lines its author wrote, and the hook's verbatim path judges them, so trimming them all in the history makes the two paths judge different texts again

git reads a shallow clone's boundary commit as a root, so `--root` answers its WHOLE tree as its own diff (measured: curry/b haiku/a where the full clone says curry/b) — and attribution then finds a carrier for anything (t-esm5)

the gates half: with the boundary's whole tree read as its diff, a --depth 1 clone passes a shared-only ^ at 0 in silence where the full clone refuses it at 3, and the walk moves every line the tree touches (both measured)

a true root commit inside a shallow clone has no parent to be cut off from — git lists it in .git/shallow all the same — and its tree IS its diff, so refusing every commit git reads as parentless leaves a real root unattributed; the object's own header is what tells the two apart (measured)

the fail-loud gate is the ONLY guard left on an unread range (t-pysg replaced the per-arm refusals with it): without it a walk missing a `:boom:` pull retags a v1.0.0 draft down to v0.1.1 and a none verdict deletes the rolling draft, both at a green exit, on the very reading the walk just said it could not trust (t-441z)
glyph never publishes and never tags: writes are draft-only so a human is always the one who cuts the tag, and that is the whole safety net behind the direct git-cliff flip

FirstParentLog returns FEWER than n commits near the root by contract, and the loop after this indexes mains[i] by the LISTING length — so on any repository whose main is shorter than the pull that landed on it (every first release) a rebase-merge PANICS

with nothing left for an alignment to answer about — a pull that listed no commits, or a merge-button listing ancestry already placed whole — the canonical commit may be a sha this checkout does not hold, so falling through turns "there was nothing to align" into an exit-4 git error mid-walk

a listing is not all-verbatim or all-rewritten: a stacked pull carries its base pull's merge-button-landed commits beside its own rebased ones, and stopping at the first commit placed by ancestry left every rewritten one ungoverned by the range — measured minor out of work released a tag ago, exit 0, no warning, notes citing pre-rebase shas main does not contain (t-7h15)

a rebase does not replay the base-merge commit that "merge main into the branch" leaves, and GitHub permits rebase-merge over one — so letting it hold a position in the alignment window makes the length wrong and abandons the mapping WHOLE, taking with it every commit that could have been placed (t-7h15)

core.hooksPath relocates a repository's hooks and the family's older repos point it at a tracked scripts/hooks, so a doctor that reads .git/hooks inspects a file git never runs — and reports a clean bill of health over the stale hook in the directory git actually uses

git cleans an EDITED message (strip: comments out, cut at the scissors line) and a `-m`/`-F` one only of whitespace, so a hook that assumes the editor ran drops lines git records — the hook blessing a subject CI then rejects, measured in both directions

githooks(5) guarantees only the GIT_EDITOR=":" side: with core.editor or $EDITOR supplying the editor git leaves GIT_EDITOR UNSET in the hook (measured), so reading unset as "no editor" puts those developers on the whitespace branch, where the editor template is never stripped and every commit is malformed-subject at the hook

git cuts at the scissors line under commit.verbose with or without an editor, so a hook that cuts only when an editor ran judges the cut line and everything under it on every -m, -F and --amend --no-edit commit made under commit.verbose — measured in all six modes (t-3p3k (2))

-v reaches no hook, and under it git writes its own cut line and the whole diff into the editor's buffer, so cutting only on what a hook can see judges that diff as the message of every git commit -v — a `$`-anchored one-line subject refused at the hook though git records exactly that one line (measured)

git merge cleans with verbose 0 whatever commit.verbose says, and its own MERGE_MSG is what tells the hook a merge from a commit; read as a commit, a typed cut line opening the merge's message cuts everything and the hook stops a merge git records (measured under commit.verbose, and under --edit in the default mode)
commit.verbose=-1 is git's 'unspecified' and git commit does not cut under it (measured); read as on — as --type=bool reads it, printing true — the hook cuts an -F message at a line git keeps

bite acts on Go diffs and the smoke reads no YAML, so without the dist-gate job a reusable/action/goreleaser fix ships with zero tests again — the measured pre-gate state (t-5dbh), restored by deleting the one step that runs the gate. The job's checkout stays on purpose: a patch deleting the whole job must carry the dependabot-owned checkout SHA in its deleted lines, and then stops applying on every SHA bump (t-7zy2 — glyph#88/#89/#90 all went red that way)

restore "exactly one of app/binary" and the live-fire range can no longer call this reusable at all, so it goes back to firing a hand copy that drifted three glyph releases behind the workflows around it (t-kcm4)

drop one macOS step's artefact condition and it runs on the ubuntu runner a verdict-only caller lands on — invisible to every artefact-shipping caller, red only in the one repo whose job is to notice breakage first

a change that reached main twice — its original sha landed by another pull, or its patch already upstream of the rebase — must keep the landing git states: re-pointing the entry at the copy this pull wrote loses the released landing, and when the two straddle the base tag the range counts the change again, t-8xsb one shape over (t-nsww)

the exit-code contract has three full prose homes and the compiler sees none of them, so a row deleted from one is invisible while every remaining row stays correct — which is how the copies got out of step in the first place: README carries the exit-4 refusal clause today and DESIGN and the glossary did not

lint.yml's jq is the fleet's only machine test for a convention violation and jq matching nothing exits 1 into a guard that tolerates it, so a stale integer is silent in both directions — every real violation loses its commit-format hint and every infra failure can gain one — and a membership-only check passes it, because the stale integer is itself a real contract code

exit 4 stopped meaning only I/O the day the release command began returning it for an incomplete walk (t-pysg) and for the published floor — deliberate refusals with nothing broken underneath — so a copy that says only API/git/IO tells the next author a refusal needs a new integer, and a new integer in a frozen machine API is a breaking change every fleet repo's lint gate branches on

one machine format must have ONE flag name: --ndjson never emitted NDJSON — printCompact writes a single object — and the split cost every caller a memorised spelling per subcommand, measured as version --json and bump --ndjson BOTH exiting 2 with unknown flag; enumerating the flag from the command tree is what makes a third spelling fail here instead of in a caller's shell

pflag reports Changed as true for an explicit --json=false, so reading the machine flag by MENTION hands JSON to the caller who just declined it — and it compiles, because an unread package-level var is legal Go, so nothing but this test stands between the mistake and a caller parsing a human line

move the stale-draft deletes back above the write and a delete spends the run's ONLY chance to land the notes — measured on a permanent 503, the run burned the shipped 1s/4s/16s schedule, exited 4 and sent the PATCH zero times — and the mirror image returns with it: a failed write then leaves the strays already gone, so the run destroys state and lands nothing

convergence bookkeeping outranks the verdict again: a stale DRAFT GitHub will not delete turns a release whose notes ALREADY landed into exit 4, which release.yml's status gate reads before the verdict — so the repository stops shipping artefacts while its notes are correct, over state the next run re-derives and re-converges

the leniency is subordinate to a write that SUCCEEDED, and extending it to the none verdict — where the delete is the entire action — means a run that did nothing at all reports fine, leaving a residual draft standing for a release glyph has decided is not due

the mention fence is Line's LAST pass over the assembled line and the only one left callable, so a String that returns its bytes unfenced turns every composed notes line and preview cell into a potential live @mention — a notification to a stranger (t-hykw), shipped fleet-wide

the v2 note.line renderer routes every substituted value through Line, so a Line that stops fencing rewrites shipped notes into ones that link and notify strangers — this is the artifact-level witness

a create whose answer is lost goes back to replaying blind, and a draft has no tag for GitHub to collide on — so every replayed POST mints another identical draft, up to four siblings from one spent schedule for a human to pick through, and on an incomplete walk nothing ever converges them away

below: exists because at tag-push the new tag IS the highest v* tag — drop the strict bound and the resolver answers the tag being cut (an empty walk, so every release ships the placeholder body) or walks backwards from a higher tag, the silent-wrong-verdict class 012bfba killed in the binary

an awk over git tag --sort=v:refname answers the predecessor question with a refname sort, not a version order — a prerelease tag comes back as the base (released commits re-folded into the notes) or the predecessor comes back EMPTY (the job dies behind a tag that already exists), and no Go test can see a defect living in shell (t-s5n4)

the untagged arm is the one resolution with no tag to bound it and release.yml runs it on every push of a repository that has not released yet — drop the cap and a resolved --since-tag silently pays one API round-trip per commit of the WHOLE history (four fleet repositories measured walking everything on the v0.11.1 rollout), burning the Actions token budget on a walk nobody asked to be unbounded

a moving glyph ref inside the caller's composite action passes doctor — the consumer shape DESIGN §6 recommends escapes the one check whose header names that miss as its single unaffordable failure mode

blank the verdict's target and the dry run goes back to answering the same bytes for every --target — the preview stops naming the commit the eventual tag points at, so a typo'd sha first surfaces on the real write

the same goreleaser run has already pushed the new version to the tap, so a draft release is a window where `brew install` fetches a 404 asset until a human remembers to publish — cifail v0.1.1 sat broken for 17 days, and the revert is one word CI stays green over (1015774)

--retry 3's ~7s window measurably lost to a real GitHub outage (504x4, t-yj1b) and this action fronts every fleet repo's lint/pr-verdict/release — a shrunk width is invisible until an outage turns the whole fleet red at once (bcd93e3)

without -f curl exits 0 on an HTTP error and saves the error page as the file (measured 2026-09-29: a missing release asset fetched without -f exits 0 and writes the 9-byte body `Not Found`), so a missing asset or an outage that outlives the retries fails a step later inside the checksum check — as a mismatch (the alarm for a tampered binary) or as no checksum line at all — instead of at the HTTP status, in every fleet repo at once (t-0j9r)

README, DESIGN §6 and the action's own description promise the tarball is checked against checksums.txt AND its provenance — delete the one line that pipes it into sha_check and the install goes on unchecked with `go test ./...` green, because every token the old guard searched for lives on in the two sha_check() definitions (t-0j9r)

`if true || gh attestation verify …` keeps every word the old guards searched for on the very line while the verify never runs — with gh stubbed to fail the loop made zero gh calls and went on to the tar step (measured 2026-09-29), so every fleet job installs a tarball nothing proved glyph's release workflow built, all gates green (t-0j9r)

the fifth failed verify must exit 1 — delete that exit and the loop simply runs out and the next line extracts the tarball onto PATH (with gh stubbed to fail: exit 1 after five calls as written, the tar step reached at exit 0 with the line gone, measured 2026-09-29), fail-open under a comment that still says it hard-fails (t-0j9r)

the release tarball carries LICENSE and README.md beside the binary (measured on v4.2.0's darwin_arm64 asset, 2026-09-29) and the extraction directory goes onto PATH for the caller's later steps — drop the member and the whole archive, today's two files and whatever GoReleaser's default archive files add later, lands on every fleet job's PATH (t-0j9r)

one operator in front of the pipeline — `cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && true || grep …` — leaves the checksum line whole for any guard that reads lines while it never runs, and a tarball checksums.txt does not vouch for installs and runs at exit 0; the line-matching guard t-0j9r first wrote passed it

`sha_check() { … -c - || true; }` keeps the call and both tools' names and throws away the tool's verdict, so a mismatching tarball installs: what the install owes is that a mismatch FAILS the step, not that a checksum tool runs (t-0j9r)

`… goreleaser.yml || true; then` on the verify's continuation line reads every failed attestation as a pass — the first failure breaks the loop and the tarball installs — the natural way to silence a flaky gate, and invisible to a guard that reads the call's first line (t-0j9r)

the attestation loop wrapped in `if false; then … fi` keeps every line of the gate byte for byte and runs none of it — zero gh calls, then the install — so the gate is held by whether it runs, which no line match can see (t-0j9r)

extraction and the `glyph version` smoke moved above the checks run the downloaded binary — in a step whose env holds GH_TOKEN — before the checksum or the attestation looks at it; the step still fails afterwards, so its exit code cannot tell, and only the marker the binary leaves does (t-0j9r)

`set +e` turns every check into a log line: a 404, a mismatch and a failed attestation each print and carry on to the install. Dropping only the -e from `set -euo pipefail` is not this edit — GitHub runs `shell: bash` as `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`, so errexit is on before the script's first line, and the harness passes that edit unchanged (measured 2026-10-04, t-0j9r)

`|| true` after the tarball's curl keeps -f and throws away what it reports: a missing asset then fails a step later inside the checksum check instead of at its download — the misdiagnosis install-download-saves-an-error-page exists to prevent, reached without touching -f (t-0j9r)

the harness executes the action's one step, so a check moved into a second step that `if: false` skips is invisible to it and runs in no fleet job — the action stays one step under `shell: bash`, with no `if:` or `continue-on-error:` deciding whether its checks count (t-0j9r)

glyph notes exits 1 on an infra-only range by contract, and a bare invocation under set -e turns that verdict into a job abort behind a tag that already exists — no binaries, no cask, no attestation (7d8d733)

Go's -X ignores an unknown symbol with exit 0 and zero warnings (measured), so a moved package or renamed var ships every released binary reporting "dev" while build.yml's plain go build smoke is structurally blind to it

a SIGTERM landing in the hooks read is the operator aborting the run, and a guard that asks only the API read launders it into exit 4 with the abort rendered as commit-msg-hook could-not-run — the one code the fleet wrappers retry, so CI retries a run its operator stopped (the same signal in the API read exits 130 with nothing written)

a draft a human tagged vNext wears the v but is not the house shape, and without the ParseVersion arm the upsert adopts it — a none verdict DELETEs the human's work, a release verdict overwrites its tag and body with glyph's and files the rest as strays, and the same listing feeds the dry run, so the preview lies identically

a range that judged NO commit exits 0 exactly like a clean pass, so a stale base, an unfetched ref or an all-bot push reads as "every commit OK" — drop the verdict and the gate is back to reporting success over work it never looked at, which lint.yml only ever guarded for one cause and only on the caller side of the pin

git lists only the commits a shallow clone holds, so a range reaching past its boundary is judged in part, and silent that partial verdict reads exactly like a whole one — measured, a --depth 2 clone judged 2 of 6 commits and exited 0 with nothing said where the full clone exits 3 (t-esm5)

lint WARNS on a shallow checkout and keeps its verdict about the commits it judged: refusing would be a new lint semantics, and a shallow walk is a warning to every reporting command and exit 4 to release alone (DESIGN §4.1)

a range read is a range read: bump --range lists its commits with lint's git log, and read past logRange on a --depth 2 clone it printed a version at 0 with nothing said where the full clone refuses the range at 3 (measured)
notes --range read past logRange on a --depth 2 clone rendered 2 of 5 commits at 0 with nothing said — release notes that read like the whole range (measured)
under [[packages]] bump and notes --range read through rangeLines, and past logRange a shallow clone named only its boundary commit, never that the range itself was cut short (measured)

a reusable job id is the second half of the check-run context 21 fleet repositories require on main (measured 2026-08-10, under two different caller halves), so renaming one never goes red here — the required context simply stops reporting and every one of those repositories blocks on a check that will never arrive

:construction: is legal mid-branch and illegal at the merge, so blocking it on a topic branch makes the branch unpushable and the only escape is --no-verify — the one that turns the whole gate off, traded for a rule the merge would have caught anyway

without the remote-tracking tips the range is the branch's whole history: every commit the remote has held for weeks is re-judged on every push, and on a repository with pre-glyph history that is a hook that can never be satisfied

git writes the null oid at the repository's object width, so a 40-char test reads a sha256 repository's DELETE as a real push of a commit that does not exist — an exit 4 on `git push --delete`, on the shape a width test looks obviously correct for

the pre-push script is installed once into ~34 clones and nothing refreshes one, so arithmetic put there goes on computing the OLD range in every repository forever — and a wrong range is a wrong verdict, not a loud failure

a commit the remote already holds on ANOTHER ref still arrives on the default branch when pushed there, and excluding every remote tip removed it from the range — measured against a real `git push`, a :construction: commit pushed to a topic branch first then to main was let through in silence by the one gate that exists to stop it

only a glyph-written hook whose bytes have MOVED is drift: a current hook and somebody else's standing choice must both stay silent, or the notice fires on every commit in every repository and becomes the noise that trains people to stop reading warnings

lint.yml no longer rebuilds per-finding annotations from the envelope — the binary is the ONLY writer of the ::error:: lines a reviewer acts on, so dropping this loop loses every per-commit pointer fleet-wide while the exit code, the envelope and the whole suite stay green

a topic branch is judged by the pull_request arm as the merge candidate it becomes and a push there is mid-branch and rewritable, so a push arm without the default-branch guard lints every branch the day any caller widens its trigger — duplicating the PR gate or annotating commits that never land, at the pin, in every repository at once

a refusal downgraded to exit 0 is the silent pass wearing a warning: ref creation has no base and a force push hides exactly the rewritten commits, so "linting" either range answers green over work never looked at — the defect class the push arm exists to close

default-branch history is immutable, so a gating verdict there is a red that can never be made green — the permanently red check trains the fleet to stop reading its own gate, which costs every OTHER verdict the gate ever renders

a push from a ref other than the default branch is refused, never skipped: the pull_request arm is its judge, and the refusal names the caller's one-line trigger fix — downgraded to exit 0 it ends the step green before glyph runs, so a widened trigger passes every topic-branch push with the fix unread in a green log (a refusal the wording-keyed loop never covered, t-0j9r)

a pull_request payload with an empty base or head is refused rather than linted as the empty range `..` collapses to — downgraded to exit 0 it greens the merge gate itself, the one arm whose verdict gates, on a pull it never read (t-0j9r)

the catch-all refuses every event the step does not support, merge_group included — downgraded to exit 0 a caller wiring a new trigger gets a green check that linted nothing on every such run, and nothing red ever says the gate is not running (t-0j9r)

the empty-SHA refusal's condition made `if false` leaves its echo and exit 1 intact and unreachable: a pull_request payload with empty SHAs reaches `glyph lint --range ..`, which exits 0 having linted nothing (measured 2026-10-04: exit 0 and a "nothing linted" warning over a repository whose last commit violates the convention), and the merge gate goes green (t-0j9r)

`continue-on-error: true` on the range step keeps every line of its script and every refusal in it, and the job passes whatever the script exits — every fleet repo pinned to that tag gets a lint check that is green whatever its commits say; nothing that runs the script can see a step-level key (t-0j9r)

a squash attributes the landed commit to the pull's author, so a bot's title is excluded exactly as a bot's commit is — judge it and every dependabot pull, a daily fleet-wide event whose titles are not the bot's to change, reds a gate whose code lint.yml forwards verbatim

the squash title is the one merge-candidate subject the BASE..HEAD range can never hold, and losing its step reds nothing — the range job stays green while 158 measured fleet subjects' worth of hole reopens, resurfacing only as silently dropped bumps in later release walks

a probe that sailed through at exit 0 is the whole finding — current bytes over a glyph that cannot answer, every commit on that machine going unlinted — and reporting it as pass restores exactly the confidently-wrong byte-compare verdict this check was built to break
same decision asserted end to end: doctor must exit 3 and annotate when the fired hook waves a violation through, or the one tool that can notice a dead local gate greets it with a green report

the probe must fire the byte-identical hook and ONLY that one — never firing leaves the check answering "nothing to fire" about a hook it should be exercising, and firing the other arms runs code a read-only diagnosis does not vouch for (a foreign hook is its owner's to run)

a three-commit cleanup becomes three separate red runs, each revealing the next — the walk knows every unparsable commit before it fails and choosing to name one is pure withheld information, measured as an agent re-running lint in a loop over what bump had already seen

the walk read the whole range and the verdict is correct, so without the pre-write size gate the run spends its one chance to land the notes on a POST GitHub always 422s — exit 4 after the retry schedule instead of before it, with the operator reading an API failure where the real answer is "cut an intermediate tag"

the workflow posts the --json body verbatim, so an untruncated preview turns into a 422 at the sticky-comment POST — the advisory surface that exists to be refreshed every push goes silently missing on exactly the oversized PRs that most need a verdict

a pull TITLE that mentions "#99" would count as GitHub citing pull 99, so the one-way live oracle starts passing on citations nobody made — the drift detector for the novel hop goes vacuously green one prose mention at a time

workflow_call plumbing defaults to "" at every dropped layer without failing the run, and "" is the contract's own NOT COMPUTED — so a deleted job mapping hands every caller empty verdicts that read as a legitimate skip, and the gate a caller built on level never fires again

a single workflow_dispatch from a topic branch then rewrites the ONE rolling draft and retargets it at that branch tip, and every downstream check stays green — the unmerged commits resolve to no merged pull request and are classified from their own subjects on the direct-push arm, walkFacts stays complete so the exit-4 refusal never fires, and Publish cuts the tag on a commit the default branch never held

the four repos that hand-copy the release step — canon, dotfiles, sill, swift-toml-edit — call no reusable and carry no ref guard of their own, so this comparison is the only thing between a workflow_dispatch from a topic branch and a rolling draft rewritten from that branch: each unmerged commit resolves to no merged pull and is classified from its own subject on the direct-push arm, walkFacts stays complete so the exit-4 refusal never fires, and Publish cuts the tag on a commit the default branch never held — at exit 0

the dry-run exemption is the whole reason this guard reds nothing that was green, and it is argued AGAINST a ratified sentence in the same file (a dry run previews the real run), so it needs a defender: judging previews refuses the escape both refusal messages advertise, reds a sanctioned dispatch path in all eleven repos on the day the pin moves, and turns fleet-preflight body probe into a skip for every clone not parked on main — the instrument a tag is cut on goes quiet exactly as the guard gets stricter

arming on both witnesses is what makes inert-outside-Actions defensible instead of lazy: flip it to OR and one missing witness DISARMS the guard instead of refusing, so a step that sets env GITHUB_REF to empty — or a runner that renames one variable — turns the fleet only write-side ref boundary back into a guard-shaped comment, green, with nothing in the log to show it

t-7zt7 is the release walk's largest ratified decision: a merge-merged pull request's work rides behind its merge commit, and --first-parent on the walk's log is the one flag that hides it — every commit inside such a PR silently leaves the verdict and the notes, so merged work ships as no release with nothing red anywhere

the t-sws7 fold: a consumer interpolates .error.message straight into ::error:: and the runner parses ONE physical line, so when the fold stops a multi-line remote error (a proxy page behind an enterprise API URL) truncates the diagnosis at its first newline — the two existing t-sws7 rows defend who draws the annotations, this one defends the fold itself

lint.yml sieves the envelope out of glyph's stderr before jq — hand jq the annotated stream instead and it exits 5 behind the step's >/dev/null 2>&1, so every range-lint convention failure (each writes its per-finding ::error:: lines ahead of the envelope) loses its summary heading in silence (t-sws7)

pattern order is the whole disambiguation model: if a later pattern can steal a commit the file no longer reads top-to-bottom and a fallback rule silently outranks the specific one it was meant to back up
a config written for a future schema read with today's field meanings judges commits by rules the author never wrote, and every verdict downstream inherits the misreading

a commit no pattern claims must refuse the whole range (ratified Q2) — folded as none instead, a commit stops existing for versioning the moment a regex misses it, and no release that ships afterwards can show which one

exclude_authors exists for bots whose messages the patterns do not describe; check the author only after matching and every bot commit becomes a range refusal, turning the escape hatch into the trap it was cut for

v2 lint checks that a pattern claims the message and nothing else — one combination veto in the gate and glyph starts owning style opinions the design explicitly hands to the author, a scope that only ever grows

a commit lands in every section whose filter matches it — dedupe on first placement and section ORDER silently decides which section owns a commit, so reordering the file rewrites what the Dependencies section even means

draft_on_none is the whole reason this package exists: treat a none verdict as v1 regardless of the flag and the maintained Unreleased draft is deleted on the first quiet merge after a release, exactly the disappearing-draft the flag was ratified to prevent

an rc exists to be executed as a real fleet gate before anyone claims the fleet should move; lose these two `auto`s and the candidate takes GitHub `latest` and regenerates the Homebrew cask, so proving v3 on a real binary means shipping it to every reader and every `brew upgrade` first

goreleaser.yml hands below: the tag it is cutting and .goreleaser.yaml marks a hyphenated one prerelease, so refusing a candidate here kills the release job at exit 2 behind a tag that already exists — no notes, no binaries, no cask, no attestation, which is the exact failure below: was added to end

the claim reads the body autosquash lands, not the amend! subject — claim every amend! and a reword of a fixup! commit passes the hook with autosquash as its remedy, then autosquash lands the original commit titled fixup!, which every gate refuses and no second autosquash folds, its sigil gone until a reword (t-t84a, t-mfny; measured on git 2.54)
git's own --fixup=reword:<a fixup! commit> has to be refused at the hook, the last gate that sees it before autosquash turns it into a fixup! commit no later autosquash folds

every value note.line substitutes is the author's text and renders as prose, the scope included (DESIGN §2) — pass the values raw and a scope a repository's own pattern captured as <i title="x"> puts a live tag into a published release body, v1's incident (#61), and a subject a live link, with lint exiting 0; nothing else in the suite notices (measured 2026-09-29, t-0j9r)

the fence is sized against every backtick run, a run behind a backslash included — skip a backtick that follows a backslash and "a \\` b @bob" (the backslash escaped, the backtick live) gets a one-backtick fence that pairs with the author's backtick, so GitHub renders @bob as a LIVE mention, a notification to a stranger (t-hykw); nothing else in go test ./... notices (t-0j9r, measured 2026-10-04)

the walk base is a release HEAD's history holds — read every tag the clone carries and a checkout at an older commit folds none (a real release there DELETES the rolling draft, hand region and all), a side branch's v9.0.0 steps main to v9.1.0 over work v1.1.0 shipped, and a maintenance branch steps from the next major's tag; glyph-monorepo-test's frozen tier collapsed to none on every line at v3.3.0 (#15 there, DESIGN §4)

MergedTags is the resolver's whole reachability question — list every tag instead and a side branch's release and a tag on a blob come back as releases of HEAD's history, so the walk base is another history's tag again

an unborn history holds no tags — pass git's "malformed object name HEAD" (exit 128) through and a checkout before its first commit, where the unfiltered listing answered empty, turns bump --pr and preview --pr from exit 0 into exit 4 (measured)

a shallow checkout cannot say what its history holds — ask --merged anyway and a --depth 1 clone with its tags fetched loses every release past the depth, so v2.0.0 -> v2.1.0 reads as v0.0.0 -> v0.1.0 (measured) where it read the latest release before
a literal runs-on ignores the caller's runner input, so a repository that moved its lint or preview to its own runner keeps spending hosted minutes with nothing red anywhere
no fleet caller passes with:, so the runner input's default is where all of them run — change it and the pin move puts every repository's lint on a label most have no runner for

a status leaves the adapter only on a method whose contract documents it — let PullRequest hand its carrier out and a caller asking IsCommitUnknown of it takes a pulls/{n} validation 422 for the release walk's API lag, the silent fallback flatten exists to rule out; PullRequest and GenerateNotes both carried theirs out until t-esm5 (measured)

a 422 on a commit's file listing is the answer commits/{sha}/pulls gives for a sha GitHub does not know — hand it back unclassified and release dies on a raw API error with no remedy, bump and notes fail where they only report, and preview takes the whole verdict comment down where its rule is to say what it could not read (t-esm5, measured: exit 4 raw on all four, the scoped commit included)
CommitFiles is the third method whose status escapes on purpose — flatten it and the caller can no longer tell GitHub's 422 from an outage, so every unlisted file listing is an API failure again

a capped or 422 file listing names its own remedy, the wedge escape per line whose range holds the commit — drop it and release's refusal offers only a re-run, which never un-caps a 3000-file listing: the remedy nothing can satisfy that DESIGN §4.1 names as a defect (t-ft7p, t-esm5)

a 422 on page 2 of a commit's file listing comes after GitHub listed page 1 — hand back nothing beside it and the caller cannot keep what was read, the capped listing's rule (DESIGN §4.1; stand-in server only, no live trigger known)

throw away the files page 1 listed before a 422 and attribution runs over nothing: an unscoped ~ whose listed file is curry's leaves curry at none, and the warning says the files GitHub listed touched no package — a lower floor than the evidence read (g6 review, measured on the stand-in server)

no shipped preset may skip fixup!/squash!: a skip answers before autosquash folds the commit into its target — skip it and a --fixup whose files lie on another [[packages]] line than its target's leaves that line at none with every gate green while the autosquashed history moves it, and a --fixup of a released commit, which autosquash leaves as it is, ships its change as a silent none (t-mfny, measured 2026-09-29 on git 2.54)

the real hook and the range gates on histories git wrote: with the pair skipped the hook passes a --fixup silently, lint --range is 0 and bump leaves the fixup!'s line at none, and a fixup! autosquash cannot fold reads as no release instead of a refusal

the fixup!/squash! reason names the reword beside autosquash — drop it and a fixup! autosquash leaves as it is, its target outside the commits being rebased, is refused with a remedy the author cannot carry out, the unreachable-escape defect t-mfny was filed against (the reworded commit lints 0, measured 2026-09-29)

the reason conditions its reword on what autosquash did, not on where the target lives — condition it on the target being already merged or released and a stacked branch's fixup!, whose target sits on the parent topic, neither merged nor released, is refused at 3 with no escape that describes it, though autosquash leaves it as it is and the reword lints 0 (t-mfny review, measured 2026-10-04 on git 2.54)

a package name no read scope group can capture is a line no commit can name: accept it and rule 3's refusal offers (my_lib), which then fails every gate as matching no pattern — the refusal's one scope escape cannot be written, so a shared-only change meant for that line has no carrier but = (t-mfny, t-f2cb)
the refusal is a load error at exit 2 on every verdict command, the commit-msg hook's --message included: without it lint --range answers 3 offering a scope escape the grammar cannot spell

one read scope group spelling the name is enough, because which pattern wins is a property of each commit (note.line's union): demand every group and a scope narrowed on purpose — a literal (?P<scope>deps) — refuses every package in the file
a skip pattern's commit is placed nowhere and an unlandable one is reported unmatched, so neither scope is ever read: count them and a name only they spell loads as a line no commit can name
Match keeps a pattern's last scope group, so a name only an earlier one spells is never read: count it and the wedge this rule removes loads again

the root's name is read like any package's (rule 2 on a zero-file commit, the contradiction check): exempt its default . and the refusal offers . as an escape (measured: (one of haiku, .)) while the one scope that reaches the root line needs a name nobody was asked to set
whether a scope exists is the pattern file's decision (DESIGN §2): refuse names under a grammar that captures none and a monorepo placed by its paths alone cannot load
the path is the tag's prefix: accept a segment git's refname rules refuse and bump prints a b/v0.0.1 at exit 0, a tag git cannot create, with doctor green on the path (t-f2cb, measured 2026-09-29)

git tag refuses a tag name that begins with -, though git check-ref-format accepts it: accept such a path and bump prints -dash/v0.0.1 at exit 0, a tag no one can cut with git tag, the remedy the wedge refusals print (t-f2cb, measured 2026-10-04)

skip is total — a skipped commit is in no section — so a group only a skip pattern captures binds for no rendered line: count it and $branch from a Merge pattern loads clean and renders empty on every line, the resolves-empty-forever template the loader exists to refuse (t-f2cb, measured 2026-09-29)

the raw-line fallback binds $subject for every commit no pattern claims, whatever the patterns name their groups: leave it out of the legal set and a file whose subject group is title is refused the one name that renders a bot line's text, so its release body drops that text with no spelling that keeps it
the fallback and the loader key off one name: refuse $subject at load and the only template that renders both a title-grammar commit and a bot's first line does not load

the fallback binds $subject only for a commit no pattern claims, so where no pattern captures subject it completes a template and never carries one: accept it as the only group cited and the gemoji preset with its group renamed to title loads, printing every matched commit's line with its text gone at exit 0, where adfc5e1 refused it (t-f2cb, measured 2026-10-04)

a trailer outranks a group at render, so one named subject replaces the fallback's text on every bot line: accept it and a title-grammar file renders each such line as "- " at exit 0 (measured 2026-10-04)

a trailer name is refused for meaning two things on a rendered line, and a group only a skip pattern captures binds on none: read every pattern's groups and that name is refused for a meaning it never has, the trailers and note.line reading two different sets

every command reads the glyph.toml at the checkout's top level, so init writes it there: write the current directory and init from a subdirectory leaves a file nothing reads at exit 0 while the missing-config remedy sends the author back to init, a loop (t-f2cb, measured 2026-09-29)

a signal during init's top-level read is the user's abort: read it as outside a checkout and init writes ./glyph.toml at exit 0 after the Ctrl-C, from a subdirectory the file nothing reads (measured 2026-10-04: exit 0, where the arm exits 130 with nothing written)

a version field past 2^31-1 is no version glyph reads: accept it and Next wraps a field at the int ceiling, printing v-9223372036854775808.0.0 as the next version at exit 0 (t-f2cb, measured 2026-09-29)
--current past the cap is usage and a tag past it leaves the walk base's candidates: accept either and bump steps a wrapped version at exit 0, from the flag or from the highest tag

a caller file doctor cannot read is unknown, never skipped: skipped, chmod 000 on a failing caller turns the startup-death check into a pass whose observation says no caller exists — bytes nobody saw, reported as an observed absence (t-fdd8 (3))

with no loadable glyph.toml the fired lint exits 2 before judging anything and the hook waves 2 through as 0, so failing that 0 tells the reader to repair a PATH wrapper nothing observed broken while the real cause sits in glyph-toml-loads (t-fdd8 (5))

end to end with the hook glyph writes: a checkout missing glyph.toml, a glyph that exits 2 like the real one, and commit-msg-hook-fires must stay unknown pointing at glyph-toml-loads instead of failing over the wrapper

attribution matches git's path strings, so a path that only the filesystem opens as a directory — a case-different spelling on APFS, a symlink git records as a 120000 blob — claims no file, and a stat-based check passes the very typo it exists to name (t-fdd8 (1))
end to end on one history: lint --range refuses a commit under haiku/ at 3 as touching no declared package, and doctor must not call the same Haiku / currylink declarations healthy
the listing is trees only: list blobs too and a declared path that names a file or a symlink reads as a subtree, the shape package-paths-exist exists to fail

HEAD's tree listing runs after the tag read, so a signal landing there is carried by treesErr alone — a guard that forgets it launders the operator's abort into package-paths-exist could-not-run at exit 4, the code the fleet wrappers retry

GitHub runs a composite from wherever it sits and a root action.yml is the published action every consumer runs, so a scan that stops at .github/actions passes tools/installer/action.yml and a root action.yml pinning @main (D2b, measured at adfc5e1)

git still lists a tracked action file the working tree deleted, and its absence is observed: read as unreadable, the pin check goes unknown and doctor exits 4 over a checkout whose every executing file was read (D2b review, measured)
a sparse-checkout entry is tracked but its bytes were never put on disk: read as a working-tree deletion, a composite nobody read passes the pin check as an observed absence
GitHub reads action.yaml as readily as action.yml, and the pin check reads only what the listing hands it: drop one spelling and every composite written that way pins @main unread

a composite in an initialized submodule is code the checkout runs, and a tracked listing without --recurse-submodules lists only the gitlink — a regression of a moving pin the filesystem walk used to catch (D2b review, measured)
end to end: a composite inside a submodule under .github/actions pinning @main must fail doctor at 3, as it did before git listed the files

the action-file listing runs after the tree listing, so a signal landing there is carried by actionErr alone — a guard that forgets it launders the operator's abort into workflow-glyph-pins could-not-run at exit 4, the code the fleet wrappers retry

a caller starts against the reusable at its own pin; judging every pin by this binary's tables fails lint@v1.0.0 callers granting exactly what v1.0.0 declares and blesses release@v0.4.0 callers omitting the app v0.4.0 required (D2a, measured at adfc5e1)
a stamped glyph older than the pin knows nothing the newer release declares, so trusting its tables passes a caller missing a grant or input added since

a call into a reusable this glyph has no row for — one added after it was built — is unjudged, not absent: skipped, a notes.yml@v5.0.0 caller passed as "no workflow calls a glyph reusable … observed — not assumed" (D2a review, measured)

a caller with no permissions block is the repository default's at any pin, so the exemption must run before the pin rule — the other order turns every block-less caller at an old pin unknown and exits 4 over a healthy caller

run the doctor of the release you pin is a remedy only from the release the check shipped in: glyph v0.4.0 has no doctor and v1.0.0's has no caller checks, so offering it below the floor sends the reader to a check that does not exist (D2a review)

an unreleased build (dev, a pseudo-version, build.sh's git-describe stamp) names no upper end and trusts its own tree — read the stamp as its base triple and a tree built past v4.2.0 calls every pin above v4.2.0 could-not-run, the releases it was built to judge

a current pre-push hook proves its script, not the glyph it resolves on PATH, and only the commit-msg probe asks that: with nothing fired beside it, an unqualified pass vouches for a gate that may let every push through (t-2etd (b))
end to end with pre-push installed alone by name over a broken glyph: the report must say nothing was fired, as a notice that leaves the exit at 0

the pre-push hook refuses a violation only on the default branch it reads from refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD, and without that ref warns and exits 0 on every push: a pass there vouches for a gate that can block nothing (t-2etd (c))
end to end on a real clone: a remote added without its HEAD must surface as advice naming the remote and `git remote set-head <remote> -a`, and stop once the ref is recorded

with a current pre-push hook the remote-heads read is the last git read, so a signal landing there is carried by headsErr alone — a guard that forgets it launders the operator's abort into pre-push-hook could-not-run at exit 4, the code the fleet wrappers retry

a remote name config accepts and refs refuse can record no default branch, and git answers it 128 where an absent ref answers 1 — read that as a failure and every caller's nothing-recorded arm is unreachable for that remote

end to end: one hand-edited remote name turns pre-push-hook could-not-run and an all-green machine's doctor exits 4, which the fleet's wrappers read as retryable infrastructure, over a remote the hook can block nothing on either
